label: Contributor 01 built and refined Lantern’s tablet-side offline scan workflow, supported its trial and handover, and helped define—but did not finish—the cross-device conflict response. The limited trial continued and was later approved for a modest expansion, while broader adoption and causal impact remained unproven.

themes.name: Personal implementation scope
themes.criterion: Conclude that Contributor 01 owned the tablet event-flow slice and implemented the persistent offline queue, device event IDs, retry behavior, visible pending state, and tests; do not attribute the service or labels to them.
themes.pitfall: Calling Contributor 01 the sole creator of Lantern or crediting them with the service endpoint, reporting table, labels, or firmware.

themes.name: State model and constraint adaptation
themes.criterion: Identify Contributor 01’s scan-state draft and their adaptation to the handheld limitation by moving event-ID generation to the tablet, while recognizing Contributor 03 surfaced the constraint and Contributor 02 added server uniqueness.
themes.pitfall: Presenting the design as entirely unilateral or claiming the handheld generated event IDs during the trial.

themes.name: Review-driven retry correction
themes.criterion: Note that the initial retry implementation risked battery drain and Contributor 01 corrected it after Contributor 06’s review by capping automatic retries and adding a permanent-rejection test.
themes.pitfall: Omitting the initial defect or treating the correction as proof that no operational risk remained.

themes.name: Trial preparation and execution evidence
themes.criterion: Credit Contributor 01 with drafting the trial checklist and documenting week-one observations, while preserving the non-random two-lane scope, weak comparison basis, and unavailable raw export.
themes.pitfall: Generalizing the 612 accepted events or 47 delayed uploads to the whole depot, or claiming the inaccessible export independently verifies more than the retained notes.

themes.name: Operator wording response
themes.criterion: Conclude that Contributor 01 responded to observed rescan confusion by changing the queued-state wording and shift card; supervisors later reported improvement only across two lanes and three shifts.
themes.pitfall: Claiming a depot-wide usability improvement or confusing suppressed same-device replays with all duplicate scans.

themes.name: Shared causes and rollout deferral
themes.criterion: Distinguish the supplier label failure and training-capacity constraint from tablet behavior; Contributor 01 proposed expansion, but Operations deferred it and retained a limited trial.
themes.pitfall: Blaming Contributor 01 for every delay, or saying their proposal itself caused a rollout.

themes.name: Known cross-device gap
themes.criterion: State that event-ID deduplication did not prevent equivalent scans from separate devices. Contributor 01 analyzed the tradeoff and proposed a banner but left implementation blocked on service design and an operations resolution workflow.
themes.pitfall: Claiming Contributor 01 fixed cross-device conflicts, or treating the unresolved item as evidence that the entire queue failed.

themes.name: Handover and continuity
themes.criterion: Credit Contributor 01 with documenting diagnostics, badge meanings, and limitations and handing routine releases to Contributor 04; subsequent routine releases used the runbook without changing the queue.
themes.pitfall: Treating later releases as Contributor 01’s work or implying their rotation ended all involvement.

themes.name: Observed outcomes without causal overclaim
themes.criterion: Report that the two trial lanes continued operating, replacement labels improved in a small wash sample, and May collection records moved from 34/40 to 38/41, but dispatch differences and paper fallback prevent causal attribution to Lantern.
themes.pitfall: Claiming Lantern or Contributor 01 definitively improved tote recovery rates.

themes.name: Later decision and remaining adoption uncertainty
themes.criterion: Conclude that by the horizon Operations approved adding two south lanes in August based on stable queue operation, replacement labels, and trainer availability; this remained an expanded trial, not west-depot or general adoption, and collection impact was uncertain.
themes.pitfall: Calling Lantern fully launched, using the post-horizon four-lane update as an in-horizon outcome, or presenting expansion as solely caused by Contributor 01.

themes.name: Background and distractors
themes.criterion: Recognize the older paper-process delay as context and disregard unrelated facilities and social messages when assessing Contributor 01’s contribution.
themes.pitfall: Mistaking coincident operational messages for Lantern work or omitting the older process context entirely.

author_note: This is a wholly fictional, pre-frozen evaluation corpus. It provides message, document, and repository evidence but no interviews, device telemetry beyond retained summaries, or accessible raw lane export. Later outcomes are intentionally limited and multi-causal; the post-horizon August update exists to test temporal discipline.
